Brand guide
Present Atomic clearly.

Use the full logo where space allows. Use the standalone symbol for compact placements such as avatars and icon grids.
Colour and type
Logo violet#5959E6
Campaign accent#5C32F7
Ink#1F152C
Soft background#F4EAFF
Manrope is the campaign typeface. The supplied wordmark is outlined vector artwork, so recipients do not need to install the font. The logo’s canonical violet is preserved; the brighter purple is the campaign accent. The font licence is included in the assets folder.
Space and legibility
Leave clear space of at least half the symbol’s height around the full logo. As a practical starting point, use the full lockup at 120 pixels wide or larger, and the symbol at 24 pixels or larger. Check legibility at the final display size.
Usage
Keep proportions and colours intact. Use the white version on a dark background and the colour or black version on a light one. Avoid stretching, outlining, adding effects or placing the mark over busy imagery. Write the product name as “Atomic” in text.

Which file should I use?
SVG: Best for web, digital publishing and design work. Scales cleanly; all wordmark lettering is outlined.
Transparent PNG: For slides, social graphics and tools that need a bitmap. Supplied at 512 and 2048 pixels wide.
Vector PDF: For print and page-layout software. RGB artwork; a printer can handle any required colour conversion.
What is in the logo folder?
Lockup: symbol and wordmark together.
Wordmark: the lettering alone.
Symbol: the atom graphic alone.
Each is supplied in colour, black and white.
Editorial credits
Suggested credit for product screenshots and campaign artwork: “Courtesy of Atomic / Abstract Machines.” Suggested credit for team portraits: “Courtesy of Abstract Machines.” The kit does not identify individual photographers.
Sample-app photographs appear within product screenshots. Those screenshots are supplied to illustrate Atomic; the embedded photographs are not supplied as separate stock assets. Preserve context and avoid implying the sample businesses are customers.
